details:
Q1: How much of the recommendation should this fix cover?
Choices:
A) Only the hard deny: refuse protected automation paths in `override_guard` for `scope-blocked`, plus contract tests (RECOMMENDED)
B) A, and also require every override path to appear in the scope guard's rejected-path list. That list would be parsed from the trusted pipeline-login scope-blocked comment, which needs a new structured marker in `implement_handle_guard_block.sh` and evidence plumbing in `unblock_judge.sh`
C) B, and also check where the issue's existing `files_touched` scope came from (only scope written by a trusted author or the pipeline can be extended)
Q2: Which repositories should the scope-override hard deny apply to?
Choices:
A) Every repository, the same as the existing destructive-latch deny-list ("in any repository") (RECOMMENDED)
B) Only `shubhodeep1/coding-workflows`, the same as the existing `FORBIDDEN_OVERRIDE_PREFIXES` check; consumer repos keep today's behaviour
Q3: Which paths should a scope override always refuse?
Choices:
A) `PROTECTED_AUTOMATION_OVERRIDE_RE` (`.github/`, `.claude/`, `workflow-templates/`, case-insensitive) in every covered repo, plus the existing source-repo-only `scripts/` prefix (RECOMMENDED)
B) A, plus `CANONICAL_SOURCE_RE` (`agents.md`, `ai_pipeline.md`, `unattended_system_instructions.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `prompts/`, `scripts/`, `.github/ai/`, `.github/scripts/`)
**Note:** B together with Q2:A would also block overrides for ordinary `scripts/` and `prompts/` application code in consumer repos. Pick Q2:B if you want B, or the plan will need re-clarification.
